svg.text: Three Ways to Make Code Thread-Safe
The safest shared state is state that can't be corrupted — these three approaches build toward that
Thread-Safe
Design
Design so shared mutable state is coordinated — or avoided entirely.
Confinement, guarding invariants, safe publication, and choosing the right strategy per
field. The umbrella skill: knowing what "correct under concurrent access" requires.
Immutable
Objects
The strongest guarantee: state that never changes can't race.
If an object can't be modified after construction, it's automatically safe to share across
any number of threads with zero locking. The default you should reach for first.
Thread-Safe
Dependency
Injection
Wire shared components so singletons don't hide unsafe mutable state.
Singleton-scoped beans are shared by every request thread. Keep them stateless or
immutable; scope anything mutable correctly. Applies the first two ideas to real apps.
The through-line: prefer no shared mutable state → if you must share, make it immutable → if it must change, coordinate access.
Deep lock mechanics, race-condition anatomy, and deadlocks each have their own dedicated topic later in Step 3.
